STEP 1 - Scene: This is a single whole apple (red-yellow skin) resting on a white dish or basin. The photo is taken from below and slightly to the side, so the apple looks closer and larger than it is.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white vessel is roughly 20 cm across, judged as a side-plate-sized dish. The apple's width is about 0.28 of the vessel's width, which gives about 5.5 cm. Because the apple sits closer to the camera, I use about 6.5 cm as a compromise.

STEP 3 - Items: One item, a whole apple. No sauce, oil or other food is visible.

STEP 4 - Area: The apple covers about 25% of the dish's visible area. The dish is essentially the apple alone, so food covers only a small part of the vessel.

STEP 5 - Volume: A sphere of about 6.5 cm diameter has a volume of roughly 4/3 × π × 3.25³ ≈ 145 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole apples are slightly less dense than water because of core and air, so about 0.85 g/ml gives roughly 125–130 g. I use 130 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw apple is about 52 kcal per 100 g, so 130 g × 0.52 ≈ 68 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single medium-small apple at about 130 g and roughly 70 kcal is plausible for what is visible.

ANSWER: {"items": [{"name": "whole apple (raw)", "grams": 130, "kcal_per_100g": 52}]}
